A wide rectangular watercolor study on warm cream parchment paper with soft visible paper-fiber texture and subtle granulation across the entire surface.

A single large burnt-orange-blending-into-amber watercolor wash anchored in the TOP-RIGHT area of the composition. CRITICAL COMPOSITION RULE — THE PAINTING CONTINUES BEYOND THE IMAGE FRAME: the orange wash is larger than the visible image; the image shows only a CROP of a bigger painting. Saturated orange pigment fills and runs ALL THE WAY PAST the top edge of the image and ALL THE WAY PAST the right edge of the image — the image boundary CUTS THROUGH the middle of deeply saturated pigment along those two edges, so when viewed the pigment appears to bleed off the page and continue beyond the frame. There is NO tapered watercolor edge, NO feathered fade, and NO clean parchment visible along the top edge or along the right edge of the image — those two edges are entirely inside saturated orange pigment. The wash ONLY fades and feathers on its INWARD-facing sides, where it transitions softly into clean parchment toward the bottom-left portion of the composition — torn feathered edges, natural pigment pooling and back-runs, and granulation occur only along this inward fade, never at the image boundary.

The wash occupies roughly the upper-right third to half of the composition. The lower-left majority of the composition is entirely clean untouched cream parchment paper showing only the paper's own fiber texture — no pigment, no stains, no secondary washes.
